question: What do BSP's disclosed deals show?
html:
The disclosed deals point to theme-first buying: a sector studied first, then an anchor portfolio company bought in a banked process, either from another sponsor (larger checks) or from founders taking their first institutional capital (smaller checks). This is read from public announcements, not from BSP's internal criteria (BSP deal record).

Thesis before the deal

  • Deal releases present each company as the result of sector work done in advance. RJ David spent "over a year" in electrical services before CET, and Adam Glucksman tracked accounting before Smith + Howard (BSP deal record).
  • Since 2024 every anchor deal has been in essential services: Punctual Pros, Frontline and CET. Fair Harbor is the only discretionary consumer company (BSP deal record).

Two kinds of seller

Seller typeExamplesPattern
Sponsor secondaryThomas Scientific (Carlyle, Jan 27, 2022), BPI (Svoboda), Frontline (BV, Dec 11, 2024)Outgoing sponsor often rolls a minority. Inherited CEO replaced at about 13-15 months
Founder or partner ownerFair Harbor, Smith + Howard, Punctual Pros (Apr 3, 2024), CET (Feb 2025)First institutional capital. Founder CEO stays
  • CEO changes followed the secondary pattern: Simmons to Haas at Thomas, and Naidoo to Britt at Frontline. Britt was appointed Jan 27, 2026 (BSP firm profile).
  • Founder CEOs Sean Taylor, Matt Buckwalter and John Duquette Jr. stayed (BSP deal record).

Banked, repeat advisers

  • Six of seven anchor deals had a named sell-side adviser. Punctual Pros went to "eight finalists" (BSP deal record).
  • Berenson advised BSP on Thomas, BPI, Frontline and CET. Harris Williams advised on Punctual Pros and Frontline. Morrison Cohen or Greenberg Traurig was counsel on every deal (BSP deal record).
  • Structures adapt to the sector. At Smith + Howard, BSP invested in the advisory LLC while the CPA firm kept attest work (BSP deal record).

Capital and add-ons

  • Fund I shows $335M sold on Form D. The $50-250M check range is unverified (BSP firm profile). Small fund size means deals lean on co-invest (Private-equity landscape).
  • Financing varies. Thomas used an Apollo/MidCap unitranche maturing December 2027. Fair Harbor shows no debt on public record (BSP deal record).
  • BSP states 23 add-ons. Twenty-one are identified by name (BSP deal record).

Gaps in the record

  • Entry multiples, equity/debt splits and screening weights are not in the context. Deal memos or IC materials would answer them.
  • CET's seller was not disclosed (BSP firm profile).
  • Two add-ons are unnamed: one at Punctual Pros, one at Smith + Howard.
  • The check-size band and the Fund I close are not confirmed in fund documents.
